reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents a Ludo application as a way to earn unlimited daily Paytm cash, including a stated ₹625 wallet amount, while describing paid participation in which ₹10 can be paid to receive ₹18. It also shows entry and win amounts with Add Money and Withdraw controls, requests account and personal details during signup, and directs viewers to a Telegram giveaway. The records do not establish whether payments, rewards, data misuse, or the external giveaway actually occurred.

before playing Ludo You can earn 625 in Paytm wallet
how to play Ludo and how to earn money
You will pay ten rupees and will get Rs.18
here you earn to buy your coin 10, 25, 50 rupees directly from your Paytm

opening.argument: The earning language is conditional rather than a guarantee. The speaker ties the stated reward to winning a Ludo match and explains that the outcome depends on which player wins. The video therefore describes a risk-bearing game promotion, not an assured payment scheme. Its claims should be read as contingent examples of possible winnings, with viewers expected to understand that participation and success are required. The records do not establish that every viewer is promised, charged, or guaranteed a particular return.

citations.quote: if you won one game you will get 60 rupees daily on this app
if that person will win then he will get 18 rupees
when we will win so guys we will get an entry fee

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats promotional figures as proof of a scam, but its own cited language is conditional: winning is the stated trigger, and the ₹10-to-₹18 example is a game outcome rather than a promised return. The opening also concedes that the records do not establish whether payments or rewards occurred. That uncertainty supports treating this as a contingent promotion rather than certifying it as fraudulent.

citations.quote: if you won one game you will get 60 rupees daily on this app
if that person will win then he will get 18 rupees

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Conditional wording does not cure the central representation. The video still advertises the application as a way to earn unlimited daily cash and presents specific wallet and payout amounts. A game can have conditional wins while still being used to solicit paid participation. The absence of proof that a payment occurred does not negate the promotional claim itself.

You will pay ten rupees and will get Rs.18

opening.argument: The content is best understood as an operational demonstration of how the Ludo application works. The speaker walks through signup, game selection, entry amounts, gameplay, wallet funding, and withdrawal steps, explicitly presenting the subject as an application whose operation is being explained. The sampled interface shows the Ludo Province screen, bet-selection menu, gameplay board, and wallet controls, consistent with a tutorial or product demonstration. Explaining how a service functions is not, by itself, evidence that the service is deceptive.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution describes the walkthrough as solicitation, but the cited material also shows an instructional sequence: signup, game operation, and payment navigation. A demonstration can quote the application's advertised rewards without independently guaranteeing them. The records do not show that the creator verifies, fabricates, or conceals any result, so the tutorial framing remains plausible.

citations.quote: First You have to type your account After you type you have to fill your name then your mobile number then your date of birth
So, now I will tell you how to play loulou

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is not neutral merely because it explains steps. It repeatedly tells viewers they can earn cash, directs them to download the application, and explains how to add money and withdraw. Those instructions operationalize participation in the claimed earning scheme, rather than merely analyzing or testing it.

citations.quote: I have given the link to this application in the description
here you earn to buy your coin 10, 25, 50 rupees directly from your Paytm
then it will be easier for you to pay payment in your Paytm

opening.argument: The observable mechanism is an ordinary paid gaming service with selectable entry fees and stated prizes. The interface presents multiple bet levels, a two-player game, and corresponding win amounts; it also includes standard wallet functions for adding funds and withdrawing them. Nothing in the supplied record establishes a deposit-only scheme, downline recruitment, credential theft, or guaranteed investment return. Signup fields and payment controls are ordinary operational features of an app and do not, without evidence of misuse, establish a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: you can add more even you can go into plus and go to Admin here you can do y here you earn to buy your coin 10, 25, 50 rupees directly from your Paytm

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies paid entry and wallet controls, but those features are also consistent with ordinary skill-game commerce. It does not show a deposit-only mechanism, recruitment structure, or misuse of the signup information. The stated Telegram destination is a promotional giveaway request, not proof that the application itself is fraudulent.

citations.quote: Application link - Join Telegram 500Rs GiveWay Paytm

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The ordinary-commerce framing omits the inducement: viewers are told to pay entry amounts to obtain larger stated winnings and are promised rapid Paytm receipt. The interface's Add Money and Withdraw controls corroborate a cash-linked flow, while the records do not establish that the service actually pays. Lack of evidence for every possible scam mechanism does not make the observed earning claim ordinary.
